items.title: 61521_David Albert Francis oral history interview
items.q: Now we were liable to play any of Sousa's marches

ctx.x: Now, like when St. Agnes's band used to play all these funerals -- we would meet at the hall, at the rehearsal hall where the band used to rehearse at, which was the parish hall of St. Agnes Church. We would meet there, and say, the funeral was going to start at two o'clock -- well, we would meet at 12:30, the band would meet there, and naturally you belonged to a couple of lodges -- at least one lodge. So the band would assemble at the parish hall and march down to the lodge hall, and go to the lodge hall -- all…

Now we were liable to play any of Sousa's marches, going to the lodge hall and going to the home, but now, when we leave the home with the body, we take the snares off the drum, which was a field drum, and took the snares off and took a handkerchief and put the handkerchief around the snares so there would be no vibration at all - just a dead sound.
And we would play a tune like "Free as a Bird," you know, dum da da da, da -- we would play that, or we would play "Abide With Me" -- a tune like that, and march slowly to the church.
